app.tagline: See, understand and manage all your AI coding projects.

workspace.localHint: Projects on this computer. Private by default.
workspace.allHint: Projects on this computer and from your team
workspace.teamHint: Projects shared through your team hub
workspace.pickerTip: Switch workspace: this computer, your team, or a server

stop.title: Emergency stop
stop.body: This stops every running agent, scheduled job and remote command right away.

palette.placeholder: What do you want to do?

projects.title: Projects
projects.emptyBody: God Eye finds your projects automatically from your Claude Code sessions. Start a session in any project and it appears here.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.emptyBody: Approvals, mentions and alerts will show up here.
inbox.notice_overlap: a teammate is in the same files
inbox.useTip: Open a new chat with this text ready to send
inbox.notice_lesson: A lesson keeps coming back: make it a rule?
inbox.notice_opinion: Changed its mind after new evidence
inbox.notice_update: New major version of a package you use

placeholder.body: This page is planned. See plan.md for the details.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Turkish and English are ready. Other languages will be prepared for you the first time you pick them.
settings.modeSimpleHint: Only what you need, in plain words.
settings.keymapVimHint: j/k to move, gg/G to jump, / to search.
settings.systemHint: Tools God Eye can use on this computer.
settings.autoSummarizeHint: Finished sessions are summarized in plain words with a small, cheap model on your own account.
settings.toneHint: Plain is for anyone; technical names files, functions and tools.
settings.enhanceHint: Turns short, lazy requests into clear prompts using what God Eye knows about your project. Uses the small, cheap model.
settings.enhanceTip_off: Never offer it (the enhance button is hidden too)
settings.enhanceTip_suggest: Show a small hint under short or vague prompts
settings.enhanceTip_auto: Short or vague prompts open the enhancer before they're sent
settings.enhanceLangTip_en: AI tools follow English prompts best; you still see explanations in your language
settings.enhanceLangTip_user: Keep the prompt in your own language
settings.themeNotionTip: A warm, quiet light theme like Notion
settings.textSizeHint: Makes everything bigger, including icons and spacing.

onboarding.readyBody: God Eye runs only on your computer. Nothing leaves it unless you decide to share.

project.noReports: No reports yet. They are written automatically for days with activity, or you can ask for one now.
project.renameHint: Only changes the name shown in God Eye.
project.gitFlowHint: Work on your own branch, open a PR to main, and deploy only main. When on, God Eye asks before you commit straight to main. Code on servers comes only from git.

memory.title: Project memory
memory.hint: What God Eye remembers about this project. It is given to every new AI session, so the AI starts from the facts instead of guessing.
memory.empty: Nothing remembered yet. Memory fills in as sessions get summarized.
memory.addPlaceholder: Something every AI session should know…
memory.conflictBody: A newer session said something different. Which one is right?
memory.conflictTeamBody: Two people on the team recorded decisions that can't both hold. Agree on one; your choice is shared with everyone.

setup.hooksTitle: Give new sessions the project memory
setup.hooksBody: Adds a small hook to this project's local Claude Code settings. Every new session then starts with the memory above. Your repo is not changed: the file stays out of git.

session.noSummaryBody: This session has no summary yet. God Eye can write one in plain words.
session.missing: Edited files that no longer exist
session.missingHint: The AI changed these files, but they are not on disk anymore. They may have been moved or deleted.
session.older: Only the latest messages are shown.
session.claims: Said it worked, right after a failure
session.claimsHint: The AI said this right after a step failed. Check it before you trust it.
session.packagesHint: Checked against the public registry (npm, PyPI).
session.pkgWarn: AI sometimes invents package names, and attackers publish packages with those names. Check this one before using it.
session.inView: What the AI has in view
session.inViewHint: Files it read or changed most recently.
session.memoryOn: Project memory was given at start
session.memoryOff: Project memory is not given to sessions (turn it on in Setup)
session.mentioned: Files the AI mentioned that don't exist
session.mentionedHint: The AI wrote these paths in its answers, but there is no such file in the project. It may have made them up.

health.title: Session health
health.contextHint: How full the AI's working memory is. Above 80% it starts to forget earlier details.
health.fresh: This session is tired. Starting a new one with a summary will give better, more reliable answers.
health.compact: Half of the AI's working memory is used. Typing /compact in this session now keeps it sharp for longer.

git.title: Code flow
git.behind: Others pushed {{count}} commits you don't have. Pull before you start, so your work doesn't collide.
git.ahead: {{count}} of your commits are not pushed yet. Others can't see them.
git.changed: {{count}} changes aren't committed. Commit them before switching tasks or deploying.
git.noUpstream: This branch isn't connected to a remote branch yet.

ask.action: Ask AI about your past work
ask.noAnswer: Nothing in your sessions answers this.

mcp.title: God Eye tools inside Claude
mcp.hint: Lets Claude look up project memory and past sessions by itself, in every project.

term.title: Terminals
term.emptyBody: Start a Claude, Codex or shell session from any project. It keeps running even if you close this page.
term.forkHint: Starts a new branch of this conversation; the original stays as it is.
term.freshHint: Opens a new session that already knows what was done and what is left.
term.handToHint: Continue this work in {{tool}} with a summary of what was done and what is left.

code.conflict: This file changed on disk while you were editing. Reload to see the new version.
code.pickFile: Pick a file on the left
code.binary: This file can't be shown as text.
code.keymapTip: Which editor's shortcuts the code editor uses
code.replaceConfirm: Replace {{total}} matches in {{files}} files? A snapshot is saved first so you can undo it.
code.replaced: Replaced {{total}}. A snapshot was saved before (History).
code.blameTip: Show which session (or commit) last changed each part of this file
code.mainWarning: You're on {{branch}}. The recommended flow is to work on a branch and merge into {{branch}} with a PR. Commit to {{branch}} anyway?
code.openSession: Open the session that wrote this

files.title: Files
files.name: Name
files.addFolderHint: Full path of a folder God Eye may open
files.protected: Protected folders like ~/.ssh are never shown.
files.emptyHint: Drop files here or use Upload. Other folders can be opened after you allow them in Settings.

preview.explainAsk: Explain this file in plain words: what is it for and what's important in it?
preview.summarizeAsk: Summarize this file in 3-5 short bullet points.
preview.askSelectionQ: Explain this code in plain words.
preview.askPageQ: Explain this page in plain words.

quick.title: Quick question
quick.hint: Ask anything without touching your main session.
quick.fullHint: Uses everything the session saw (slower, uses more of your limit).
quick.explainFile: What does this file do? Explain it in plain words.

ideas.title: Ideas
ideas.empty: No ideas yet. Press Ctrl+I anywhere to drop one.
ideas.reviewTip: Once a week: which ideas to do now, which later, which to drop

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.empty: No saved prompts. Save the ones that work well and reuse them in one click.
prompts.bodyHint: Use {name} for blanks you fill in each time, e.g. {file} or {feature}.

servers.title: Servers
servers.emptyBody: Add a server you reach with ssh. God Eye uses your own ssh and ssh-agent; it never reads your keys.
servers.name: Name
servers.targetHint: user@host, a host name, or an alias from ~/.ssh/config
servers.riskHint_danger: Can delete data or take the server down. Needs a double confirmation.
servers.confirmDanger: Type the server name to confirm
servers.hostKey: First connection to this server: open the SSH terminal once and accept its host key, then check again.
servers.askDraft: Look at the server {{name}} ({{target}}, tag: {{tag}}). Last check: {{state}}. What do you see, what is risky, and what should I do first? Only read; ask me before any command that changes something.

approvals.title: Waiting for your approval
approvals.dangerCheck: I understand this can't be undone

chat.title: Chat
chat.placeholder: Ask Claude to do something… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
chat.modeHint_normal: Every step that changes something waits for your OK.
chat.modeHint_acceptEdits: File edits go through; commands still ask.
chat.modeHint_auto: Claude decides what's safe and runs it, in a separate copy of your repo. Pushing, merging and deploying still always ask.
chat.modeHint_plan: Claude only plans; nothing is changed.
chat.emptyBody: Claude works in this project's folder. Steps that change things wait for your approval.
chat.suggestTip_opus: This looks like hard or wide work; the strongest model makes fewer mistakes here (it uses more of your limit).
chat.suggestTip_haiku: A short question: the small model answers quickly and saves your limit.
chat.guard_ship: This would send your work out (push, merge, publish or deploy). AI never does that on its own, so it asks every time.
chat.guard_external: This chat read content from the internet. Text there could try to steer the AI, so risky steps are asked every time.
chat.notice_external: This chat read content from the internet. That content is treated as information, not instructions: the chat is back to asking before each step, and "always allow" no longer covers risky tools.
chat.notice_notebookRejected_one: 1 change of mind was not saved: it had no new evidence
chat.notice_notebookRejected_other: {{count}} changes of mind were not saved: they had no new evidence

checkpoint.title: Snapshots
checkpoint.hint: God Eye saves your code before every AI step. Go back to any of them.
checkpoint.restoreBody: These files will be put back as they were. Your current state is saved first, so you can undo this.

limits.title: Limits
limits.subtitle: How much of your AI limits is used, where, and when.
limits.noData: No limit reading yet. It appears after the next Claude reply in God Eye (chat, quick question or a summary).
limits.fullAt: At this pace it fills at {{time}}.
limits.safe: At this pace it lasts until the reset.
limits.switchHint: Close to the limit: switch to another account for new sessions, or hand the work over to Codex.
limits.tokensHint: Counted: new input, output and cache writes (cache reads are left out).
limits.csvTip: Download the monthly totals as a spreadsheet file
limits.emptyBody: Start a Claude Code or Codex session in any project. How much you use, and how close you are to your limits, shows up here.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.label: Name
accounts.loginHint: A terminal opens with the tool's login. Finish it there, then press Check.
accounts.noSwitch: God Eye never switches accounts on its own; you choose.

team.connectIntro: Your projects stay on this computer. Only the projects you choose to share are sent, end-to-end encrypted, to your team's hub. The hub can't read them.
team.newPasswordHint: Your invite has a temporary password. Pick your own here (at least 10 characters).
team.adminHint: For anyone with an account on the hub (the first admin too). On the team's very first sign-in, this computer creates the team key.
team.privacyE2e: Everything is encrypted before it leaves this computer; the hub only stores ciphertext.
team.privacyOff: Projects are not shared until you turn sharing on for them.
team.privacyScrub: Secrets like API keys and passwords are removed before anything is sent.
team.roleHint_admin: Can invite people, change roles and see the audit log.
team.roleHint_member: Shares and sees the team's projects.
team.roleHint_viewer: Can only watch; never sends anything.
team.shareHint: Off: nothing leaves this computer. Summaries: session titles, summaries, stats and project memory. Full: the conversations too. Secrets are always removed.
team.inviteReady: Send this code to {{name}} privately (not in a public channel). They paste it on their Team page.
team.inviteSecret: This code contains the team key. Anyone who has it can read shared projects.
team.usersHint: Who can sign in to this hub.
team.resetReady: {{name}}'s old password no longer works and their devices were signed out. Send them this new code.
team.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}} from the team? Their devices are signed out right away.
team.devicesHint: Every signed-in computer. Sign out one you don't recognize.
team.auditHint: Sign-ins and admin actions on the hub.
team.recoveryBody: This key unlocks everything your team shares. The hub doesn't have it. If every admin loses it, shared history can't be read again. Store it in a password manager.
team.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect this computer from the team? Your local data stays; teammates' shared copies stay here too.
team.signedOut: The hub signed this computer out (password reset or removed). Ask your admin for a new invite code.
team.keyMismatch: The team key on this computer doesn't match the hub. Syncing is paused. Ask your admin for a new invite code.
team.membersHint: Who is online and what they are working on right now.
team.noMembersBody: Invite teammates from the admin section below.
team.sharingHint: Choose per project what your team can see.
team.shareTip_off: Nothing from this project leaves your computer
team.shareTip_summary: Session titles, summaries, stats and project memory — not the conversations
team.shareTip_full: Everything, including the conversations, live. Secrets are always removed
team.privateOn: Kept to yourself: not shared with the team.
team.privateOff: Shared with the team like the rest of this project.
team.privateTip: A private session never goes to the hub, even in a shared project. Making it private also asks teammates' apps to remove their copy.
team.previewTip: See what the next sync sends for this project, after secrets are removed
team.previewHint: This is what leaves this computer (encrypted) for this project. Secrets are already masked.
team.previewNoMessages: Conversations are not shared at this level.
team.codeHint: Two-factor sign-in is on for this account: type the code from your authenticator app.
team.inviteNoKey: The code has no team key in it. After they join, approve their computer here (Waiting for approval).
team.signOutUserTip: Sign this person out of every device
team.clear2faTip: For someone who lost their phone
team.clear2faConfirm: Turn off two-factor sign-in for {{name}}? They can turn it on again after signing in.
team.forgotHint: If your account has an email address, the hub sends a code to it. Fill in the hub address and your username above first.
team.forgotSent: If that account has an email address, a code is on its way. It works for 30 minutes.
team.forgotNoMail: This hub can't send email. Ask your admin for a new invite code.
team.forgotDone: Password changed. Sign in now; a teammate approves this device before you see team data again.
team.emailOptional: Email (optional, for the invite and password resets)
team.mailFrom: Sent from {{from}} through the hub's SMTP
team.mailOff: Email isn't set up on the hub. Set SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASS (for example a Gmail app password) to turn it on.
team.emailFailed: The email didn't go out ({{error}}). Copy the code and send it another way.
team.editEmail: Email address for invites and password resets
team.linkedBanner: Your team shares this repo: you see their sessions and decisions here. Yours stay on this computer until you share them.

enhance.buttonTip: Turn a short request into a clear prompt with your project's context
enhance.hintTip: Adds your project's context, limits and a clear "done when". You review it before anything is sent.
enhance.title: Enhanced prompt
enhance.templateTip: The AI limit is reached or the CLI isn't available, so a template was used: your words plus the project's facts.
enhance.working: Reading your project and writing a clearer prompt…
enhance.ctxTip_memory: Decisions, conventions and "tried, didn't work" notes from earlier sessions. Click to leave them out.
enhance.ctxTip_session: The latest messages of the session you're in, so "this" and "it" make sense. Click to leave it out.
enhance.ctxTip_git: Branch, uncommitted changes and recent commits. Click to leave it out.
enhance.ctxTip_file: The file open in the editor and your selection. Click to leave it out.
enhance.ctxTip_error: The most recent error in this session. Click to leave it out.
enhance.ctxTip_team: A teammate is editing the same files right now. Click to leave it out.
enhance.questionsIntro: A couple of quick questions so nothing is guessed:
enhance.skipTip: Build the prompt from your words and the project facts, without asking.
enhance.bigJob: This looks like a big job. Starting in Plan mode lets the AI propose steps before changing anything.
enhance.assumptionsTip: Things the AI couldn't know for sure. Remove any that are wrong.
enhance.dialogPlaceholder: Write it the lazy way, e.g. "login is broken, fix it"
enhance.refiningTip: You can already use this version; the AI one replaces it when ready (unless you've started editing).
enhance.expandedTip: Your shorthands were expanded (Settings → Prompt enhancer).
enhance.saveTip: Keep this prompt in your prompt library to reuse it
enhance.ctxTip_log: The latest error printed in this project's terminal (a failing test or a crashed server). Click to leave it out.
enhance.shortcutsHint: Words you type to save time. They are expanded before the prompt is written, e.g. dyy → doğrusunu yap.
enhance.suggestedTip: Is "{{word}}" a shorthand? Click to define it.
enhance.weekly_one: This week you enhanced {{count}} prompt; {{enhanced}} went out enhanced.
enhance.weekly_other: This week you enhanced {{count}} prompts; {{enhanced}} went out enhanced.
enhance.weeklyMissing: What your own prompts most often lacked: {{part}}.
enhance.weeklyErrors: Errors in the 30 minutes after sending: {{enhanced}} with enhanced prompts, {{original}} with your own.

insight.scoreTip: {{score}}/100 · grade {{grade}}. Computed from the checks below; every point has evidence.
insight.trendEmpty: The trend appears after the next scan.
insight.reexplainTip: Write a fresh explanation (uses the small model)
insight.explaining: Reading this part of the project…
insight.diagramArchHint: Arrows: who imports whom, with the number of imports.
insight.diagramDbHint: From the migrations and schema files in the code.
insight.gainTip: Fixing this raises the score by about {{points}} points
insight.fixTip: Open a chat with a ready prompt for this. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
insight.askPlaceholder: Ask or ask for something about {{section}}…
insight.noScanBody: God Eye reads the code (nothing is run or sent anywhere) and scores each part with evidence.
insight.scanTip: Re-read the code and score again. Free: no AI is used for scores.
insight.overallHint: The average of the sections below; security and tests count a bit more.

readme.title: README at the top of the project
readme.fix: Add a README.md at the project root that says what the project is and how to run it.

bigFiles.title: Very long files: {{metric}}
bigFiles.fix: Split the longest files (over 600 lines) into smaller modules with one clear job each, without changing behaviour.

todo.title: TODO / FIXME notes: {{metric}}
todo.fix: Go through the TODO and FIXME comments: do the quick ones, turn the rest into tracked tasks, and remove stale ones.

types.title: Typed code: {{metric}}
types.fix: Convert the remaining JavaScript files to TypeScript, starting with the most used ones.

lint.title: Linter / formatter set up
lint.fix: Set up a linter and formatter (for example Biome or ESLint + Prettier, or Ruff for Python) with a config file in the repo.

strict.title: TypeScript strict mode
strict.fix: Turn on "strict": true in tsconfig.json and fix the type errors it reveals.

bigComponents.title: Very large UI components: {{metric}}
bigComponents.fix: Break the largest UI components (over 400 lines) into smaller components and hooks, keeping the UI identical.

any.title: Uses of "any": {{metric}}
any.fix: Replace "any" types with real types (or "unknown" plus a check) in the listed places.

errorBoundary.title: Error screen instead of a blank page
errorBoundary.fix: Add an error boundary (or the router's errorElement) so a crash shows a friendly error screen instead of a blank page.

i18n.title: Ready for other languages
i18n.fix: Move the UI texts into translation files with an i18n library so the app can be translated.

dark.title: Dark mode
dark.fix: Add a dark theme that follows the system setting (prefers-color-scheme) using shared color variables.

responsive.title: Works on small screens
responsive.fix: Make the layout responsive with breakpoints so it works on phones and narrow windows.

alt.title: Images without alt text: {{metric}}
alt.fix: Add meaningful alt text to the listed images (alt="" for purely decorative ones).

focus.title: Visible keyboard focus
focus.fix: Add clear :focus-visible styles so keyboard users can see where they are.

validation.title: Input validation
validation.fix: Validate request bodies and parameters with a schema library (for example zod or valibot; pydantic in Python) at the API boundary.

rateLimit.title: Rate limiting
rateLimit.fix: Add rate limiting to login and other expensive or public endpoints.

emptyCatch.title: Errors silently swallowed: {{metric}}
emptyCatch.fix: In the listed places, handle or log the error instead of ignoring it with an empty catch.

migrations.title: Database migrations
migrations.fix: Manage schema changes with versioned migrations instead of changing tables by hand.

injection.title: Queries built from strings: {{metric}}
injection.fix: In the listed queries, pass values as bound parameters instead of inserting them with ${...} (SQL injection risk).

ci.title: Automatic checks on every push (CI)
ci.fix: Add a CI workflow (for example GitHub Actions) that installs, lints, type-checks and runs the tests on every push.

dockerUser.title: Containers don't run as root
dockerUser.fix: Add a non-root USER to the listed Dockerfiles.

dockerignore.title: .dockerignore present
dockerignore.fix: Add a .dockerignore that leaves out node_modules, .git, build output and .env files.

healthcheck.title: Health check
healthcheck.fix: Add a HEALTHCHECK to the Dockerfile (or healthcheck in compose) so broken containers are noticed.

pinned.title: Base images without a fixed version: {{metric}}
pinned.fix: Pin the listed base images to a specific version instead of :latest or no tag.

envTracked.title: .env files kept out of git
envTracked.fix: Remove the listed .env files from git (git rm --cached), add .env to .gitignore, and change every secret that was in them.

secrets.title: Keys or passwords in the code: {{metric}}
secrets.fix: Move the secrets found in the listed lines to environment variables, and change (rotate) those keys, since they were committed.

publicKeys.title: Public client keys to restrict: {{metric}}
publicKeys.fix: These Google/Firebase client keys are public by design; make sure each one is restricted (app, website and API restrictions) in Google Cloud Console.

dangerous.title: Risky code patterns: {{metric}}
dangerous.fix: Review the listed eval, innerHTML, shell commands built from strings and similar: replace them with safe alternatives or sanitize the input.

exists.title: Tests: {{metric}} files
exists.fix: Add tests for the most important behaviour, starting with the code that breaks most often.

ratio.title: Test files per code file: {{metric}}
ratio.fix: Add tests for the main modules that have none yet (aim for about one test file per three code files).

script.title: One command runs the tests
script.fix: Add a "test" script (or pytest config) so the whole suite runs with one command.

ci.title: CI runs the tests
ci.fix: Make the CI workflow run the test suite, not just the build.

assets.title: Heavy files in the repo: {{metric}}
assets.fix: Compress or resize the listed assets (WebP/AVIF for images), or load them from a CDN.

lazy.title: Pages load only what they need
lazy.fix: Load rarely used pages and heavy components on demand (React.lazy / dynamic import).

readme.title: README length: {{metric}} characters
readme.fix: Expand the README: what the project does, how to install and run it, and how it's organised.

install.title: README explains how to start
install.fix: Add an "Install" and "Usage" section to the README with the exact commands.

license.title: License
license.fix: Add a LICENSE file so others know how they may use the code.

envExample.title: .env.example for settings
envExample.fix: Add a .env.example listing every environment variable the code reads, with empty or sample values.

any.title: Any documentation
any.fix: Add at least a README describing the project.

lockfile.title: Exact versions locked (lockfile)
lockfile.fix: Commit the lockfile so everyone installs the same versions.

loose.title: Unbounded versions: {{metric}}
loose.fix: Replace "*", "latest" and open-ended ">=" versions with normal ranges (for example ^1.2.3).

mixedLocks.title: One package manager
mixedLocks.fix: Keep a single package manager: remove the extra lockfiles in the listed folders.

deprecated.title: Deprecated packages: {{metric}}
deprecated.fix: Replace the listed deprecated packages with their maintained alternatives.

typecheck.title: Type check passes
typecheck.fix: Fix the type errors reported by the type check (see the output in "Run the project's own checks").

lint.title: Linter passes
lint.fix: Fix the problems the linter reports.

tests.title: Tests pass: {{metric}}
tests.fix: Make the failing tests pass, or fix the code they caught.

audit.title: Known vulnerabilities in dependencies: {{metric}}
audit.fix: Update the packages with known vulnerabilities (start with critical and high).

auditSecurity.title: Serious vulnerabilities in dependencies: {{metric}}
auditSecurity.fix: Update the packages with critical or high vulnerabilities now.

catHint.architecture: How the project is put together: its parts and how they depend on each other.
catHint.frontend: The code that runs in the browser or app: screens and components.
catHint.uiux: How it looks and feels: themes, small screens, accessibility.
catHint.backend: The server side: APIs, business rules and how requests are handled.
catHint.database: Where data is stored: tables, migrations and queries.
catHint.devops: Building, shipping and running it: Docker, CI and deployment.
catHint.security: Secrets, risky code and what could leak.
catHint.testing: How well the code is checked automatically.
catHint.performance: How fast it loads: heavy files and loading only what's needed.
catHint.docs: How easy it is for someone new to understand and start.
catHint.dependencies: The outside packages it relies on and how safely they're pinned.

apis.title: API map
apis.hint: Every outside service the code talks to and every endpoint it serves, found in the code itself.
apis.noExternal: No outside services found in the code.
apis.unknownTip: God Eye doesn't know this service by name; it was found by its URL in the code.
apis.envKeyTip: Setting this service reads (name only; values stay in .env)
apis.flowHint: Front-end → your endpoints → outside services, from the calls in the code.
apis.undocumented_one: {{count}} setting the code reads isn't in .env.example (others won't know to set it):
apis.undocumented_other: {{count}} settings the code reads aren't in .env.example (others won't know to set them):
apis.unused_one: {{count}} setting in .env.example that no code reads:
apis.unused_other: {{count}} settings in .env.example that no code reads:

what.firebase: Google's app backend: sign-in, database, files, push notifications.
what.supabase: Hosted Postgres database with sign-in and file storage.
what.aws: Amazon cloud services, often S3 file storage.
what.smtp: Sends e-mails through a mail server.
what.sentry: Collects errors and crashes from the app.
what.github: Reads or changes things on GitHub.
what.cloudinary: Stores and resizes images and videos.
what.replicate: Runs AI models in the cloud.

apis.tryTip: Send a request to this endpoint and see the answer
apis.testerHint: Sent from this computer. Fill in path parameters like :id before sending.
apis.baseTip: Where your API is running (read from PORT / API_URL in your .env when there is one)
apis.healthTip: Calls every GET endpoint without parameters once and shows the status code

env.title: .env and secrets
env.privacy: Values stay on this computer. They are never sent to AI or to your team, and never written to logs.
env.syncTip: Add every setting name to .env.example (names only, never values) so others know what to set.
env.noneBody: Create one to keep this project's settings and keys out of the code.
env.addHere: Add this setting to this file
env.removeConfirm: Delete {{key}} from {{file}}? A backup is kept.
env.historyHint: A copy is saved before every change. Restoring also saves the current version first.
env.issue_missing: read by the code but missing in {{file}}
env.issue_format_url: doesn't look like an address in {{file}}
env.issue_format_boolean: should be true or false in {{file}}
env.linkTip: Edit the .env on one of your servers next to the local ones (over SSH)
env.linkHint: Choose a server you added on the Servers page and the full path of its .env file. It's read over SSH; values only come to this computer.
env.remoteTip: Read and written over SSH. A dated backup is kept on the server before every change.
env.unlinkConfirm: Stop showing this server file here? Nothing is deleted on the server.
env.restartHint: Running services read .env when they start. Restart the service so it uses the new values.
env.restartDanger: This command is marked dangerous. Run it anyway?

tools.title: Run the project's own checks
tools.hint: These run your project's code on this computer (type check, linter, tests, dependency audit). Check the commands, then start them. The results count toward the scores for two weeks.
tools.runTip: Starts the checked commands one after another. The emergency stop button stops them.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.tip: Choose how much each part counts and turn off checks that don't fit this project
scoring.hint: The overall score is the weighted average of the parts. A weight of 0 leaves a part out. Turned-off checks don't count.
scoring.enableTip: Turned off: click to count it again
scoring.disableTip: Click to turn this check off for this project

import.title: Bring in this project's history
import.estimate: {{sessions}} past sessions have no summary yet. Summarizing them fills the project memory: about {{tokens}} tokens with the small model ({{model}}), around {{minutes}} min.
import.startTip: Uses your own Claude login; nothing else is sent anywhere.

firewall.found_one: This message seems to contain a secret ({{hints}}).
firewall.found_other: This message seems to contain {{count}} secrets ({{hints}}).
firewall.hint: AI tools keep conversations. Mask it unless the AI really needs the value.

deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.typeName: This is production. Type "{{env}}" to confirm.
deploy.failed: The deploy failed (exit {{code}}). Nothing was rolled back automatically; see the output.
deploy.unknownCommit: The server's commit isn't on this computer (fetch first)
deploy.serverAheadBy_one: server has {{count}} commit this computer doesn't
deploy.serverAheadBy_other: server has {{count}} commits this computer doesn't
deploy.dirty_one: {{count}} file was changed directly on the server (outside git)
deploy.dirty_other: {{count}} files were changed directly on the server (outside git)
deploy.workflowTip: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys here whenever the branch changes
deploy.workflowHint: This file will be added as {{path}}. Add the secrets it names in GitHub; nothing is pushed for you.
deploy.workflowWritten: Created {{path}}. Commit and push it when you're ready.
deploy.removeConfirm: Remove this environment from God Eye? Nothing changes on the server.
deploy.noneBody: Add the server where this project runs (Staging or Prod) to see what's deployed and deploy safely.
deploy.noServers: Add a server first on the Servers page.
deploy.addHint: The project on a server, as a git checkout. God Eye never copies code; the server pulls it from git.
deploy.name: Name
deploy.check_serverDirty: Files were changed on the server outside git. Commit or undo them there first, or they'll be lost or conflict.
deploy.check_serverBranch: The server is on another branch
deploy.check_serverAhead: The server has commits this computer doesn't. Pull first.
deploy.check_unpushed: You have commits that aren't pushed; the server won't get them
deploy.check_noUpstream: This branch has no remote; the server can only pull what's pushed
deploy.check_uncommitted: Uncommitted changes here won't be deployed
deploy.check_testsUnknown: Tests haven't been run here recently (Sections → Run the project's own checks)
deploy.check_testsFailing: The tests failed the last time they ran
deploy.check_envMissing: Settings the code needs are missing in the server's .env:

remote.saveConfirm: Save {{path}} on the server? A dated backup is kept next to it.

sync.repairTip_one: {{count}} event from a teammate is missing; fetching it again
sync.repairTip_other: {{count}} events from teammates are missing; fetching them again
sync.brokenTip_one: {{count}} event didn't link to the one before it
sync.brokenTip_other: {{count}} events didn't link to the ones before them

keys.waiting: You're in. An admin now needs to approve this computer before it can read the team's work; this happens on their God Eye, usually within minutes.
keys.requestsHint: These computers signed in but don't have the team key yet. Approve only devices you recognise: approving lets them read everything the team shares.
keys.rotateHint: Replace the key after someone leaves: new updates use a new key only the remaining devices get. Older history stays readable for those who already had it.
keys.rotateConfirm: Make a new team key now? Every current device gets it automatically. You'll get a new recovery key to keep.
keys.rotateAfter: {{name}} no longer has access. Replace the team key too, so their devices can't read new updates? (Recommended)

alerts.title: Security alerts
alerts.hint: Sent by the hub while you're online.
alerts.new-location: {{user}} signed in from a new address: {{ip}}

policy.title: Security rules
policy.hint: Apply to everyone on this hub.
policy.sessionDays: Sign devices out after this many days unused (0 = never)
policy.retentionDays: Keep updates on the hub for this many days (0 = forever)
policy.ipAllow: Allow sign-ins only from these addresses (empty = anywhere)

access.title: Project access
access.hint: Leave a project open to the whole team, or pick who can see it. Viewers can't share in it. Admins always have access.

account.title: Your account
account.hint: Your name and colour on the team, two-factor sign-in and your devices.
account.required2fa: Your team requires two-factor sign-in. Turn it on below.
account.scan: Add this key to an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password…), then type the 6-digit code it shows.
account.signOutOthersConfirm: Sign out every other device signed in to your account?

people.idle: {{name}} is online, not working on anything shared

person.summarizeTip: A short summary of their week, in your language (small model)
person.quietBody: Their shared projects had no sessions or decisions in the last 7 days.
person.todayHint: What teammates did today in shared projects.

comments.title: Comments
comments.placeholder: Write a comment, @ to mention someone

teamwork.suggestTip: Send {{name}} a prompt idea for this session
teamwork.handoffTip: Give this session to a teammate with a ready summary to continue from

zen.exitTip: Bring back the side bar, top bar and status bar (Ctrl+Alt+Z)

langpack.generating: Making the language pack with your Claude login: {{percent}}%
langpack.ready: Language pack ready. It works offline.
langpack.none: No language pack yet. Texts show in English until it's made.
langpack.partial_one: {{count}} text isn't translated yet (shown in English).
langpack.partial_other: {{count}} texts aren't translated yet (shown in English).
langpack.makeTip: Translated once by Claude Haiku with your own login (a few minutes), then saved on this computer
langpack.fixHint: Click a text to correct it. Your corrections are kept on this computer and win over the pack.
langpack.undoTip: Go back to the original translation

translate.tip: Translated automatically from your teammate's language

errors.offline: Can't reach God Eye on this computer. Check that it's still running, then press Try again.
errors.signedOut: Your session here ended. Reload the page to continue.
errors.notFound: This isn't here anymore. It may have been deleted or moved.
errors.tooMany: Too many tries in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.server: Something went wrong on our side. Press Try again; if it keeps happening, restart God Eye.

session.text: A conversation with an AI coding tool, from your first message to the last.

token.text: A small piece of text, about ¾ of a word. AI tools count what they read and write in tokens.

context.text: Everything the AI is keeping in mind right now. When it gets full, the AI starts forgetting earlier parts.

compaction.text: When the context is full, the tool shortens the conversation to keep going; details can get lost.

hub.text: A small server your team runs. It passes encrypted updates between you and can't read them.

e2e.text: Data is locked on your computer and only unlocked on your teammates' computers. Nobody in between can read it.

recoveryKey.text: A long code that unlocks your team's data if every device is lost. Keep it in a password manager.

twoFactor.text: Besides your password, a 6-digit code from an app on your phone.

commit.text: A saved snapshot of your code changes, with a short note about what changed.

branch.text: A separate line of work in Git, so changes don't touch the main code until you merge them.

push.text: Sending your saved changes (commits) to GitHub or another shared place.

deploy.text: Putting a new version of your app on the server where people use it.

staging.text: Staging is a test copy of your live app; Prod is the real one people use.

ssh.text: A secure way to run commands on another computer, such as your server.

env.text: A file with settings and secrets (passwords, keys) for your app. It must never be shared.

worktree.text: A second working copy of the same repo, so an agent can work without touching your files.

mcp.text: A standard way for AI tools to use other programs. God Eye offers one so Claude can read your project memory.

diff.text: The exact lines that were added or removed in a change.

blame.text: Shows, line by line, who last changed the code and when.

hook.text: A small script a tool runs at certain moments, for example when a session starts.

endpoint.text: One address of your API, like GET /users.

api.text: How programs talk to each other: one asks, the other answers with data.

ci.text: Checks that run automatically on every push, such as tests and lint.

rateLimit.text: How much you can use an AI tool in a time window (for example 5 hours or a week).

persona.text: An AI teammate with a role, such as "Security expert", with its own rules and focus.

tour.title: Quick tour
tour.hint: A one-minute look at where everything is.

nav.title: Everything in one strip
nav.body: Projects, terminals, files, servers, inbox, ideas and more. Hover an icon to see its name.

search.title: Ask or jump anywhere
search.body: Press Ctrl+K: search sessions, open a project, or ask a question about your work in plain words.

inbox.title: What's waiting for you
inbox.body: Approvals, terminals waiting for an answer, warnings and messages from your team, most urgent first.

account.title: Your AI accounts and limits
account.body: See how much of your Claude or Codex limit is used. When you're close, switching to another account is one click.

stop.title: The emergency stop
stop.body: Stops every running AI job and terminal at once. Nothing else is touched.

settings.title: Make it yours
settings.body: Language, theme, text size, Simple or Pro mode, and how much AI runs in the background.

panel.resizeTip: Drag to resize, or use the arrow keys. The size is remembered.

copy.banner: Working in a separate copy on branch {{branch}} (from {{base}}). Your folder isn't touched until you merge.
copy.mergeTip: Bring these changes into your branch. Nothing is pushed.
copy.mergeConfirm: Merge the changes from this copy into {{branch}} on your computer? Nothing is pushed.
copy.merged: Merged into {{branch}}. Push it yourself when you're ready.
copy.discardConfirm: Stop this chat and delete its copy and branch? Changes that weren't merged are lost.
copy.sandboxOn: Shell commands also run in a sandbox (limited files and network).
copy.sandboxOff: For a full sandbox (limited files and network) install bubblewrap and socat.

ai-engineer.name: AI Engineer
ai-engineer.role: Builds with AI models: prompts, agents, evals

pm-lead.name: Team Lead
pm-lead.role: Splits the work, assigns it, follows it to done

database.name: Database Expert
database.role: Data that stays correct and fast

security.name: Security
security.role: Finds what an attacker would; only reads

performance.name: Performance
performance.role: Measures first, then makes it fast

devils-advocate.name: Devil's Advocate
devils-advocate.role: Finds the weak points of a plan

tech-writer.name: Technical Writer
tech-writer.role: Docs and summaries people can follow

ceo-coach.name: CEO Advisor
ceo-coach.role: Strategy, focus and what to say no to

legal.name: Legal and Compliance
legal.role: KVKK, GDPR, licenses (information, not legal advice)

rnd-engineer.name: R&D Engineer
rnd-engineer.role: Tries new tech, answers with evidence

persona.title: Persona team
persona.intro: Experts who have worked in their field all their life. Each keeps a notebook of its opinions and only changes its mind with new evidence. Talk to one, or ask several at once in a team meeting.
persona.scoreNote: Decisions kept: meetings it joined whose decision went into project memory. Bugs caught and acceptance rates come once the task board exists (Faz 8).
persona.exportBody: Writes each persona as a file your AI tools read on their own: Claude Code sub-agents (.claude/agents) in a project, or Codex custom prompts. Files are overwritten on the next export.
persona.exportCodex: Writes to the prompts folder of your Codex account; run one with /<persona id> in Codex.
persona.notebookEmpty: Nothing written down yet. Opinions appear here after chats and meetings.
persona.chatPick: In which project? The persona reads that project's memory and its own parts before it starts.
persona.f_idHint: a-z, 0-9 and dashes; used as the file name when exported
persona.f_web: May search and read the web (the chat then asks before every risky step)
persona.f_categories: Parts of the project it owns
persona.englishNote: The profile is written in English because the models follow it best. The persona always answers in your language.
persona.timelineHint: One per line: year — event. Only real, well-documented milestones.
persona.readingLibrary: Add the books you own: the persona then quotes them with the page.
persona.rulesHint: Extra rules for this persona only, one per line.
persona.rulesAll: Every persona also follows the expert rules: stay consistent with the notebook, change its mind only with new evidence, name sources, never invent numbers, rank by importance, give a confidence level.
persona.showPrompt: Show what it reads before it starts
persona.notebookHint: Claim, reasoning, evidence, confidence and date. A change needs new evidence; without it the old opinion stays.
persona.safetyNote: No persona pushes, merges, publishes or deploys on its own: those always wait for you.
persona.wizardTitle: Describe the persona in a sentence
persona.wizardBody: The AI drafts the whole profile: background, history of the field, reading list, checklist and traps. You check and change it before saving.
persona.wizardHint: For example: a payments expert who has run checkout for online shops in Europe for 15 years
persona.draftCheck: Check the draft, especially the years and books, then save.
persona.reviewTip: {{name}} looks at this part and reports what matters most
persona.reviewDraft: Review the {{section}} part of this project. Start with the open checks, then use your own checklist. List findings by importance with the file and line, say what to fix first, and give a confidence for each.

unit-tester.name: Unit Test Writer
unit-tester.role: Small, fast tests for each piece

integration-tester.name: Integration Tester
integration-tester.role: Checks that the parts work together

e2e-tester.name: End-to-End Tester
e2e-tester.role: The key user journeys in a real browser

load-tester.name: Load Tester
load-tester.role: What happens when 1000 people come at once

pentester.name: Security Tester
pentester.role: OWASP Top 10, only your own app, local or staging

cross-browser-tester.name: Browser and Device Tester
cross-browser-tester.role: Chromium, Firefox, Safari; phone to desktop

chaos-tester.name: Chaos Tester
chaos-tester.role: What if the database goes away or the network drops

meeting.title: Team meeting
meeting.question: What should the team weigh in on?
meeting.questionHint: For example: should we add sign-in with Google, and what would it change?
meeting.teamHint: suggested from your question; change it freely
meeting.leadNote: The team lead reads every answer and writes the decision.
meeting.deciding: The team lead is weighing the answers…

testers.title: Test users
testers.intro: Ordinary people, not experts, try a task in your app in a real browser and think aloud while they do. Each runs in its own private browser, on its own device size, eyesight and connection. Use it only on your own app.
testers.noBrowser: Chromium or Google Chrome is needed on this computer for test users. Install it and reload this page. (The Docker image does not include a browser to stay small.)
testers.notLocal: This address is not on this computer or your local network. Test only apps you own; the test users act on whatever is there.
testers.task: What should they try to do?
testers.taskHint: For example: sign up and add your first product
testers.audienceHint: For example: Turkish mothers aged 25-35 living in Germany
testers.usageNote: Each test user is a Claude session with only browser tools: it cannot touch your files or run commands. Each one uses part of your Claude limit; at the same time means more speed and more load on this computer.
testers.auntHint: How easy it felt for people with little tech experience (0-100). Success: share who reached the goal.
testers.needProject: Pick a project for the test to send problems to a persona
testers.repeatTip: Same people, same task: did your change make it better?

aunt.name: Aunt Ayşe
aunt.who: 70, two years on a smartphone, afraid of breaking things

hostile.name: Troll
hostile.who: tries to break things on purpose

coverage.title: Test coverage map
coverage.hint: Which folders have tests and which big files have none. Uses your coverage report (coverage/lcov.info) when there is one.
coverage.static: {{tested}} of {{files}} code files have a test that imports them or is named after them.
coverage.staticNote: Without a coverage report this only says whether a test touches a file, not how much of it. For exact numbers, run your tests with coverage (for example bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov).

library.title: Library
library.intro: What your personas read: books, documents, articles, web pages and GitHub repositories. They search it before answering and cite the page or chapter. Everything stays on this computer.
library.modelBody: Searching works by words right away. To find passages by meaning, in any language (a Turkish question finding an English book), God Eye uses a small model that runs on this computer. It is downloaded once ({{mb}} MB, free) from Hugging Face.
library.drop: Drop PDF, EPUB, Markdown, text or HTML files here
library.urlHint: A web page, an X post or a GitHub repository address
library.searchHint: Try a question, as a persona would ask it
library.empty: Nothing yet. Add a book you own, a document or a page; personas will cite it.

lessons.intro: Every mistake is written down once: a failed test or build, a change that was reverted, a checkpoint you went back to, an answer you called wrong. Before similar work, the matching lessons are put in front of the AI so the same mistake isn't made twice.
lessons.empty: No lessons yet. They appear here when something goes wrong and gets fixed.
lessons.title: Lesson
lessons.preventHint: What to do next time, e.g. run the migration on a copy first
lessons.ruleHint: This keeps coming back: make it a rule?
lessons.retroTip: Personas look back on this project: what went well, what went wrong, what we learned. It goes into the library.
lessons.retroDone: The retrospective is in the library.

knowledge.intro: Each persona reads the free, public sources of its field (Hacker News, Reddit, Lobsters, Mastodon, Bluesky, arXiv, GitHub, Product Hunt, blogs). The same story from several places is merged, rated from the persona's angle (important? real or hype? does it touch your projects?), and what matters goes into its library with the date and link.
knowledge.needsAi: background AI is off in Settings, so the schedule waits
knowledge.trendHint: Mentions in the stories read this week / the weekly average of the four weeks before.
knowledge.empty: Nothing read yet. Press Read the news now, or wait for the schedule.
knowledge.compare: Compare packages (npm names, for example react, svelte)
knowledge.compareSources: Numbers from the npm registry and download API, GitHub and the Hacker News search, fetched just now.
knowledge.sourcesHint: Comma-separated. Nothing here needs an account.
knowledge.src_feeds: RSS or Atom feeds (blogs, changelogs, newsletters, podcasts)
knowledge.xNote: X has no free legal way to read it automatically: paste the link of an important post into the Library instead.
